title: My First Square
body:
Goal: make the turtle draw a square.

  1. Open starter.py in Thonny.
  2. Finish the program so the turtle draws a square: 4 sides, all the same length, turning 90 degrees at each corner.
  3. Press the green Run button to watch your turtle.

Done looks like: a closed square (the turtle ends where it started).

Extra: change the color with t.color("#0072B2") or make it bigger.

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Look at the two lines the turtle already runs in starter.py. Together they draw one side and then turn. A square is that same pair of moves, done more than once.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Copy that pair of commands under each # TODO. The first one moves the turtle forward, and the second one turns it left. Run the program and count the sides you see.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: A square has 4 sides, and the turtle already did one. Under each of the three # TODO comments, add two lines: t.forward(____) and t.left(____). Use the same numbers as the lines already in the file, so every side matches.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# My First Square
# The turtle already draws ONE side of the square.

import turtle

t = turtle.Turtle()
t.shape("turtle")

t.forward(100)
t.left(90)

# TODO: side 2

# TODO: side 4

turtle.done()
